items.stem: Why attach a confidence score to each extracted field?

options.text: So low-confidence fields can be routed to review instead of trusted blindly
options.rationale: Correct: per-field confidence drives review routing and reduces silent errors.
Confidence scoring is about reliability, not speed.
Confidence does not alter the source document.
Confidence complements a schema; it does not replace it.

items.stem: Which TWO reconciliation checks catch extraction errors on an invoice? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Line items must sum to the stated total
options.rationale: Correct: a sum check catches many extraction mistakes.

options.text: A key field is cross-checked against a second source
options.rationale: Correct: cross-source agreement flags inconsistent extractions.

options.text: Trusting the first extracted value with no check
options.rationale: No check means errors pass through silently.

options.text: Deleting fields that look wrong without review
options.rationale: Silently discarding data loses information and hides errors.

items.explanation: Correct: a sum check catches many extraction mistakes.

items.stem: An extracted field comes back with low confidence and fails a reconciliation check. What should happen?

options.text: Route the item to human review rather than accepting it automatically
options.rationale: Correct: low-confidence, failing items should go to review, not straight through.

options.text: Accept it anyway because the agent produced a value
options.rationale: Producing a value does not make it correct.
Silent dropping loses data and hides the problem.

options.text: Lower the confidence threshold so it passes
options.rationale: Weakening the threshold hides the error rather than handling it.

items.explanation: Correct: low-confidence, failing items should go to review, not straight through.
